commands.review_summary:
The PR changes Microsoft Teams federated credential resolution so blank certificate, thumbprint, and managed-identity values do not count as configured and can fall back to environment settings.

PR surface: Source +13, Tests +36. Total +49 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for the reported resolver defect: the PR provides a direct before/after invocation of the exported production credential functions, and the changed source makes the blank-value path clear. A live Microsoft Teams tenant is not needed to establish this pre-SDK resolution behavior.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow mechanical repair can retain the intended blank-value fallback without changing valid certificate-path bytes.

target.title: fix(msteams): ignore blank certificate settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Microsoft Teams federated authentication could have whitespace-only certificate settings reported as configured. Gateway startup would then try to read a certificate file whose path consisted only of spaces instead of treating the certificate credential as missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Federated certificate paths, thumbprints, and managed-identity client IDs now use one owner-local string normalizer for config-over-environment resolution. This keeps blank config values from shadowing valid environment values while leaving secret authentication and managed-identity selection unchanged.

## User Impact

Microsoft Teams setup and status now reject blank certificate configuration consistently, and a blank config field can correctly fall back to a valid trimmed environment setting.

AI-assisted.

## Evidence

Local-machine production-function proof on Node `v24.18.0`:

1. **Before / negative control against exact latest main `aaa37a0c264a9b2bc25c6d5a8e98ede130455fed`:** in a detached worktree, imported `extensions/msteams/src/token.ts`, set `appId`, `tenantId`, `authType: "federated"`, and whitespace-only config/env certificate fields, then called both exported credential functions.

   ```text
   {"configured":true,"resolved":{"type":"federated","appId":"app-id","tenantId":"tenant-id","certificatePath":"   ","certificateThumbprint":"   "}}
   ```

   This is RED: the production resolver returned federated credentials that `createFederatedApp` passes to `readFileSync`, and channel/setup callers use the resolver result as their configured predicate.

2. **After on current exact head `28d6c00b72305edb27a0ca8125f4b964dd17e186`:** imported the same exported production functions, cleared the Microsoft Teams federated-auth environment, evaluated whitespace-only config, then evaluated the same config with padded valid environment values.

   ```text
   {"head":"28d6c00b72305edb27a0ca8125f4b964dd17e186","blank":{"configured":false,"resolved":null},"fallback":{"configured":true,"resolved":{"type":"federated","appId":"app-id","tenantId":"tenant-id","certificatePath":"/env/cert.pem","certificateThumbprint":"EEFF0011"}}}
   ```

3. **Focused regression and controls on the same exact head:**

   ```text
   node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/token.test.ts
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
   Tests       23 passed (23)
   ```

   The focused file also keeps valid certificate config/env, secret credentials, system/user managed identity, and explicit `useManagedIdentity=false` behavior covered.

4. `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/msteams/src/token.ts extensions/msteams/src/token.test.ts` passed on the same exact head; `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.

Not tested: a live Microsoft Teams certificate login, because no tenant certificate credentials were available. The changed behavior is entirely before SDK/network dispatch; the proof drives the exported production credential resolver that all channel, setup, probe, graph, monitor, and send-context callers consume.
